content: 1. The co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may result in increased plasma concentrations of letermovir. This interaction necessitates careful monitoring to avoid potential toxicity. 2. Levo-ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, levo-ketoconazole can enhance the levels or effects of voxilaprevir through the same mechanism. These interactions are considered minor, but close monitoring is advised. 3. Lonafarnib, a weak P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitor, can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. This interaction may require therapy modification or close monitoring. Additionally, co-administration of lonafarnib with P-gp substrates should be approached cautiously, as even minimal changes in substrate concentrations can lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. 4. Lonafarnib can also increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir via P-gp inhibition. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Adverse reactions should be closely monitored when lonafarnib is co-administered with sensitive P-gp substrates. 5. Lonafarnib may increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. In such cases, alternative drugs should be considered, and co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and adjust the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 6. Lopinavir can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 7. Lorlatinib can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and co-administration should be avoided. 8. Mavorixafor can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Similarly, velpatasvir can increase the levels or effects of mavorixafor via P-gp inhibition. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. 9. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Mitotane can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 11. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, can increase the toxicity of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by competing for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Momelotinib may also increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. 12. Nafcillin can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 13. Nefazodone can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Nelfinavir can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Nirmatrelvir can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Omaveloxolone can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by reducing systemic exposure of sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 18. Otesecazole, a BCRP inhibitor, can increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates, including velpatasvir. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider dose reduction. 19. Velpatasvir can increase the toxicity of ozanimod by inhibiting BCRP transport, leading to increased exposure of ozanimod's active metabolites. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 20. Phenobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 21. Phenytoin can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and co-administration should be avoided. 22. Posaconazole can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Pretomanid can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B3 transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Primidone can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 25. Resmetirom can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 26. Velpatasvir can increase the levels or effects of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Co-administration is not recommended. 27. Ribociclib can increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 28. Rifabutin can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 29. Rifampin can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and co-administration should be avoided. 30. Rifapentine can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 31. Velpatasvir can increase the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting P-gp transport. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 32. Rucaparib can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 33. Sarecycline can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting P-gp transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Voxilaprevir can increase the levels or effects of seladelpar by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Voxilaprevir can increase the levels or effects of selexipag by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs with pH-dependent solubility at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 37. Sotorasib can decrease the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inducing P-gp transport. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 38. Sparsentan can decrease the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Stiripentol can increase the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting P-gp, BCRP, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended.
